vibefpmgui.terminal

The Terminal tab: your shell, in the project's folder, with exactly the environment VibeFPMGUI was started with.

The shell gets the app's environment variables as they are (only TERM is set, for the terminal, and a prompt: PS1) and is started without its startup files (zsh -f, bash --noprofile --norc, fish --no-config), which would change them: conda's "base" activation, Homebrew's or your own PATH changes. Started from an activated pixi or conda environment, the terminal is in that environment, with everything its activation set (PATH, CONDA_PREFIX, the compilers' variables...): fpm and the compilers are the ones the app uses. (So your prompt, aliases and other shell settings don't load; the prompt is a plain one, starting with the environment's name, e.g. (VibeFPMGUI) src %, as activation would show it.)

On macOS and Linux the shell runs in a pseudo-terminal read with a QSocketNotifier, so everything happens in the GUI thread; on Windows it runs through pywinpty (ConPTY), read in a thread.

The terminal is pyte (the screen: escape codes, colors, cursor) drawn by TerminalView, with scrollback, the alternate screen (full-screen programs: vim, less, htop) and reflow (long lines wrapped again when the terminal is resized) added in TerminalScreen. TerminalView handles the keys as xterm sends them (application cursor keys, function keys, modifiers), ⌘C/⌘V (macOS) or Ctrl+Shift+C/V (elsewhere) to copy and paste while Ctrl keys go to the shell, bracketed paste, selection, scrolling, and colors that follow light/dark mode.

   1"""The *Terminal* tab: your shell, in the project's folder, with exactly the
   2environment VibeFPMGUI was started with.
   3
   4The shell gets the app's environment variables as they are (only ``TERM``
   5is set, for the terminal, and a prompt: ``PS1``) and is started without its startup files
   6(``zsh -f``, ``bash --noprofile --norc``, ``fish --no-config``), which
   7would change them: conda's "base" activation, Homebrew's or your own PATH
   8changes. Started from an activated pixi or conda environment, the terminal
   9is in that environment, with everything its activation set (PATH,
  10CONDA_PREFIX, the compilers' variables...): ``fpm`` and the compilers are
  11the ones the app uses. (So your prompt, aliases and other shell settings
  12don't load; the prompt is a plain one, starting with the environment's
  13name, e.g. ``(VibeFPMGUI) src %``, as activation would show it.)
  14
  15On macOS and Linux the shell runs in a pseudo-terminal read with a
  16`QSocketNotifier`, so everything happens in the GUI thread; on Windows it
  17runs through pywinpty (ConPTY), read in a thread.
  18
  19The terminal is [pyte](https://github.com/selectel/pyte) (the screen: escape
  20codes, colors, cursor) drawn by `TerminalView`, with scrollback, the
  21alternate screen (full-screen programs: vim, less, htop) and reflow (long
  22lines wrapped again when the terminal is resized) added in
  23`TerminalScreen`. `TerminalView` handles the keys as xterm sends them
  24(application cursor keys, function keys, modifiers), ⌘C/⌘V (macOS) or
  25Ctrl+Shift+C/V (elsewhere) to copy and paste while Ctrl keys go to the
  26shell, bracketed paste, selection, scrolling, and colors that follow
  27light/dark mode.
  28"""
  29

  31import shutil
  32import signal
  33import struct
  34import sys
  35import threading
  36import warnings
  37from collections import deque
  38from pathlib import Path

  71def user_shell() -> str:
  72    if WINDOWS:
  73        return os.environ.get("COMSPEC", "cmd.exe")
  74    return os.environ.get("SHELL") or shutil.which("zsh") or shutil.which("bash") or "/bin/sh"
  75
  76
  77class Launch(NamedTuple):
  78    argv: list[str]
  79    env: dict[str, str]
  80
  81
  82# Options that keep each shell from reading its startup files (they would
  83# change the environment: conda's "base", Homebrew, PATH edits...).
  84NO_STARTUP_FILES = {
  85    "zsh": ["-f"],                         # no .zshenv, .zprofile, .zshrc, .zlogin
  86    "bash": ["--noprofile", "--norc"],
  87    "fish": ["--no-config"],
  88    "sh": [], "dash": [],                  # (read startup files only with $ENV / as login shells)
  89}
  90
  91
  92# A plain prompt (the startup files that would set one aren't read): the
  93# folder's name, after the environment's name when one is active.
  94PROMPTS = {"zsh": "%1~ %# ", "bash": "\\W \\$ ", "sh": "$ ", "dash": "$ "}
  95
  96
  97def shell_launch() -> Launch:
  98    """How to start the user's shell with exactly the app's environment:
  99    the same variables (only TERM is set, for the terminal, and PS1, the
 100    prompt), and no startup files to change them."""
 101    shell = user_shell()
 102    env = dict(os.environ)
 103    env["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"
 104    if WINDOWS:
 105        return Launch([shell], env)
 106    name = Path(shell).name
 107    if name in PROMPTS and "PS1" not in env:  # (fish has its own prompt function)
 108        active = environment_name()
 109        env["PS1"] = (f"({active}) " if active else "") + PROMPTS[name]
 110    return Launch([shell, *NO_STARTUP_FILES.get(name, []), "-i"], env)
 111
 112
 113def environment_name() -> str:
 114    """The activated environment the app (and the terminal) runs in, if any:
 115    a pixi workspace's name (plus its environment, when not "default"), or a
 116    conda environment's."""
 117    pixi = os.environ.get("PIXI_PROJECT_NAME", "")
 118    if pixi:
 119        which = os.environ.get("PIXI_ENVIRONMENT_NAME", "default")
 120        return pixi if which in ("", "default") else f"{pixi}:{which}"
 121    return os.environ.get("CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV", "")

 124# ------------------------------------------------------------ the shell
 125class PtyShell(QObject):
 126    """A shell in a pseudo-terminal (macOS, Linux), read in the GUI thread."""
 127
 128    output = Signal(bytes)
 129    exited = Signal()
 130
 131    def __init__(self, launch: Launch, cwd: Path, rows: int, cols: int, parent=None):
 132        super().__init__(parent)
 133        self.launch, self.cwd, self.rows, self.cols = launch, cwd, rows, cols
 134        self.pid = -1
 135        self.fd = -1
 136        self._notifier: QSocketNotifier | None = None
 137        # Input the shell hasn't taken yet (it isn't reading: a long command,
 138        # a big paste); sent when the pty can take more (see _flush).
 139        self._pending = bytearray()
 140        self._write_notifier: QSocketNotifier | None = None
 141
 142    def start(self):
 143        import pty
 144
 145        argv, env, cwd = self.launch.argv, self.launch.env, str(self.cwd)
 146        program = shutil.which(argv[0]) or argv[0]
 147        with warnings.catch_warnings():  # (the child only execs: fork's thread caveat doesn't apply)
 148            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", DeprecationWarning)
 149            pid, fd = pty.fork()
 150        if pid == 0:  # the child: become the shell
 151            try:
 152                os.chdir(cwd)
 153            except OSError:
 154                pass
 155            try:
 156                os.execve(program, argv, env)
 157            finally:
 158                os._exit(127)
 159        self.pid, self.fd = pid, fd
 160        os.set_blocking(fd, False)
 161        self.resize(self.rows, self.cols)
 162        self._notifier = QSocketNotifier(fd, QSocketNotifier.Read, self)
 163        self._notifier.activated.connect(self._read)
 164
 165    def _read(self, *_):
 166        try:
 167            data = os.read(self.fd, 65536)
 168        except BlockingIOError:
 169            return
 170        except OSError:  # (Linux: EIO once the shell has exited)
 171            data = b""
 172        if data:
 173            self.output.emit(data)
 174        else:
 175            self._finish()
 176
 177    def write(self, data: bytes):
 178        """Send input to the shell, now or (what doesn't fit yet) once the
 179        pty can take more: never waiting for it in the GUI thread."""
 180        if self.fd < 0:
 181            return
 182        self._pending += data
 183        self._flush()
 184
 185    def _flush(self, *_):
 186        while self._pending and self.fd >= 0:
 187            try:
 188                written = os.write(self.fd, self._pending)
 189            except BlockingIOError:
 190                break  # (full: the rest when it's writable again)
 191            except OSError:
 192                self._pending.clear()
 193                break
 194            del self._pending[:written]
 195        waiting = bool(self._pending) and self.fd >= 0
 196        if waiting and self._write_notifier is None:
 197            self._write_notifier = QSocketNotifier(self.fd, QSocketNotifier.Write, self)
 198            self._write_notifier.activated.connect(self._flush)
 199        if self._write_notifier is not None:
 200            self._write_notifier.setEnabled(waiting)
 201
 202    def resize(self, rows: int, cols: int):
 203        self.rows, self.cols = rows, cols
 204        if self.fd < 0 or rows <= 0 or cols <= 0:
 205            return
 206        import fcntl
 207        import termios
 208
 209        try:  # (the shell gets SIGWINCH from the kernel)
 210            fcntl.ioctl(self.fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))
 211        except OSError:
 212            pass
 213
 214    def _finish(self):
 215        if self._notifier is not None:
 216            self._notifier.setEnabled(False)
 217            self._notifier = None
 218        if self._write_notifier is not None:
 219            self._write_notifier.setEnabled(False)
 220            self._write_notifier = None
 221        self._pending.clear()
 222        if self.fd >= 0:
 223            try:
 224                os.close(self.fd)
 225            except OSError:
 226                pass
 227            self.fd = -1
 228        if self.pid > 0:
 229            try:
 230                os.waitpid(self.pid, os.WNOHANG)
 231            except ChildProcessError:
 232                pass
 233            self.pid = -1
 234            self.exited.emit()
 235
 236    def stop(self):
 237        """End the shell (and what it runs), e.g. when the window closes."""
 238        pid = self.pid
 239        if pid > 0:
 240            for sig in (signal.SIGHUP, signal.SIGCONT):
 241                try:
 242                    os.kill(pid, sig)
 243                except ProcessLookupError:
 244                    break
 245        self._finish()
 246        if pid > 0:
 247            def reap():  # (no zombie: force it if SIGHUP was ignored)
 248                try:
 249                    if os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG) == (0, 0):
 250                        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
 251                        os.waitpid(pid, 0)
 252                except (ChildProcessError, ProcessLookupError):
 253                    pass
 254            QTimer.singleShot(1000, reap)
 255
 256    def is_running(self) -> bool:
 257        return self.fd >= 0
 258

 260class WinptyShell(QObject):
 261    """A shell through pywinpty (Windows ConPTY). Its reads block, so they
 262    run in a thread; the output comes back to the GUI thread as a signal."""
 263
 264    output = Signal(bytes)
 265    exited = Signal()
 266
 267    def __init__(self, launch: Launch, cwd: Path, rows: int, cols: int, parent=None):
 268        super().__init__(parent)
 269        self.launch, self.cwd, self.rows, self.cols = launch, cwd, rows, cols
 270        self._process = None
 271
 272    def start(self):
 273        from winpty import PtyProcess
 274
 275        self._process = PtyProcess.spawn(self.launch.argv, cwd=str(self.cwd), env=self.launch.env,
 276                                         dimensions=(self.rows, self.cols))
 277        threading.Thread(target=self._read_loop, args=(self._process,), daemon=True,
 278                         name="Terminal output").start()
 279
 280    def _read_loop(self, process):
 281        try:
 282            while True:
 283                data = process.read(65536)
 284                if not data and not process.isalive():
 285                    break
 286                if data:
 287                    self.output.emit(data.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(data, str) else data)
 288        except (EOFError, OSError):
 289            pass
 290        self.exited.emit()
 291
 292    def write(self, data: bytes):
 293        if self._process is not None:
 294            try:
 295                self._process.write(data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
 296            except (EOFError, OSError):
 297                pass
 298
 299    def resize(self, rows: int, cols: int):
 300        self.rows, self.cols = rows, cols
 301        if self._process is not None and rows > 0 and cols > 0:
 302            try:
 303                self._process.setwinsize(rows, cols)
 304            except (EOFError, OSError):
 305                pass
 306
 307    def stop(self):
 308        if self._process is not None:
 309            try:
 310                self._process.terminate(force=True)
 311            except (EOFError, OSError):
 312                pass
 313            self._process = None
 314
 315    def is_running(self) -> bool:
 316        return self._process is not None and self._process.isalive()
 317

 319# --------------------------------------------------------------- screen
 320SCROLLBACK = 10_000  # lines kept above the screen
 321NO_WRAP_COLUMNS = 300  # the terminal's width without word wrap (wider than the window: scroll sideways)
 322
 323# Private modes (pyte keeps them shifted, see pyte.modes).
 324DECCKM = 1 << 5                 # application cursor keys
 325ALT_SCREEN = {47 << 5, 1047 << 5, 1049 << 5}
 326BRACKETED_PASTE = 2004 << 5
 327
 328
 329class Row(list):
 330    """A line of the scrollback: its Chars (trailing blanks dropped, unless
 331    it was wrapped), and whether it was wrapped (the next row continues it)."""
 332    wrapped = False
 333
 334
 335def _wrapped(line) -> bool:
 336    return getattr(line, "wrapped", False)
 337
 338
 339class TerminalScreen(pyte.Screen):
 340    """pyte's screen, with what pyte lacks: scrollback (the lines that
 341    scroll off the top), the alternate screen full-screen programs draw on,
 342    and reflow: lines pyte wrapped at the right edge are marked, and joined
 343    and wrapped again at the new width when the terminal is resized (pyte
 344    would cut them off, or leave them wrapped short)."""
 345
 346    def __init__(self, columns: int, lines: int):
 347        self.history: deque = deque(maxlen=SCROLLBACK)  # Rows above the screen
 348        self.alternate = False
 349        self._saved_main = None
 350        self._drawing = False
 351        self.reply = lambda data: None  # answers to the terminal's queries go to the shell
 352        super().__init__(columns, lines)
 353
 354    # ------------------------------------------------------- wrapped lines
 355    def draw(self, data):
 356        self._drawing = True  # (a line feed now is pyte wrapping at the right edge)
 357        try:
 358            super().draw(data)
 359        finally:
 360            self._drawing = False
 361
 362    def linefeed(self):
 363        # Mark the row being left: wrapped (it continues on the next) or not.
 364        self.buffer[self.cursor.y].wrapped = self._drawing
 365        super().linefeed()
 366
 367    def _row(self, y: int) -> Row:
 368        line = self.buffer[y]
 369        row = Row(line[x] for x in range(self.columns))
 370        row.wrapped = _wrapped(line)
 371        if not row.wrapped:
 372            while row and row[-1] == self.default_char:
 373                row.pop()
 374        return row
 375
 376    def index(self):
 377        top, bottom = self.margins or pyte.screens.Margins(0, self.lines - 1)
 378        if self.cursor.y == bottom and top == 0 and not self.alternate:
 379            self.history.append(self._row(0))
 380        super().index()
 381
 382    def erase_in_display(self, how=0, *args, **kwargs):
 383        if how == 3:  # ("clear" also clears the scrollback)
 384            self.history.clear()
 385        rows = {0: range(self.cursor.y, self.lines), 1: range(self.cursor.y)}.get(how, range(self.lines))
 386        for y in rows:
 387            self.buffer[y].wrapped = False
 388        super().erase_in_display(how, *args, **kwargs)
 389
 390    def erase_in_line(self, how=0, private=False):
 391        if how in (0, 2):  # (the end of the line is gone: it no longer continues)
 392            self.buffer[self.cursor.y].wrapped = False
 393        super().erase_in_line(how, private)
 394
 395    # -------------------------------------------------------------- resize
 396    def resize(self, lines=None, columns=None):
 397        lines, columns = lines or self.lines, columns or self.columns
 398        if (lines, columns) == (self.lines, self.columns):
 399            return
 400        if columns != self.columns:
 401            # Tab stops every 8 columns across the new width (pyte sets them
 402            # once, for the first width: a tab past it went to the last column).
 403            self.tabstops = {x for x in self.tabstops if x < columns}
 404            first_new = (min(self.columns, columns) + 7) // 8 * 8  # (the old ones stopped before the old width)
 405            self.tabstops.update(range(max(8, first_new), columns, 8))
 406        if self.alternate:  # (full-screen programs redraw themselves at the new size)
 407            super().resize(lines, columns)
 408            self.cursor.y = min(self.cursor.y, self.lines - 1)
 409            self.cursor.x = min(self.cursor.x, self.columns - 1)
 410            return
 411        self._reflow(lines, columns)
 412
 413    def _reflow(self, lines: int, columns: int):
 414        """Join the wrapped rows (scrollback and screen) into whole lines and
 415        wrap them again at the new width, keeping the cursor on its character
 416        and the bottom of the output at the bottom of the screen."""
 417        last = max([self.cursor.y] + [y for y in range(self.lines) if self._row(y)])
 418        rows = list(self.history) + [self._row(y) for y in range(last + 1)]
 419        cursor_row = len(self.history) + self.cursor.y
 420        # Whole lines (lists of Chars); where the cursor is in them.
 421        logical, cursor_at = [], (0, 0)
 422        current: list = []
 423        for n, row in enumerate(rows):
 424            if n == cursor_row:
 425                cursor_at = (len(logical), len(current) + self.cursor.x)
 426            current.extend(row)
 427            if not row.wrapped or n == len(rows) - 1:
 428                logical.append(current)
 429                current = []
 430        # Wrap them at the new width.
 431        new_rows: list[Row] = []
 432        cursor_pos = (0, 0)
 433        for index, cells in enumerate(logical):
 434            start_row = len(new_rows)
 435            pieces = [cells[i:i + columns] for i in range(0, len(cells), columns)] or [[]]
 436            for k, piece in enumerate(pieces):
 437                row = Row(piece)
 438                row.wrapped = k < len(pieces) - 1
 439                new_rows.append(row)
 440            if index == cursor_at[0]:
 441                offset = cursor_at[1]
 442                y, x = divmod(offset, columns)
 443                if y >= len(pieces) and x == 0 and offset:  # (just past a full row: stay at its end)
 444                    y, x = y - 1, columns
 445                cursor_pos = (start_row + y, x)
 446        while len(new_rows) <= cursor_pos[0]:
 447            new_rows.append(Row())
 448        top = max(0, len(new_rows) - lines, cursor_pos[0] - lines + 1)
 449        top = min(top, cursor_pos[0])
 450        self.history.clear()
 451        self.history.extend(new_rows[:top])
 452        self.buffer.clear()
 453        for y, row in enumerate(new_rows[top:top + lines]):
 454            line = self.buffer[y]
 455            for x, char in enumerate(row):
 456                line[x] = char
 457            line.wrapped = row.wrapped
 458        self.lines, self.columns = lines, columns
 459        self.set_margins()
 460        self.cursor.y = cursor_pos[0] - top
 461        self.cursor.x = min(cursor_pos[1], columns)
 462        self.dirty.update(range(lines))
 463
 464    # ---------------------------------------------------- alternate screen
 465    def set_mode(self, *modes, **kwargs):
 466        if kwargs.get("private") and not self.alternate and {m << 5 for m in modes} & ALT_SCREEN:
 467            self._saved_main = (dict(self.buffer), self.cursor.x, self.cursor.y, self.cursor.attrs,
 468                                self.lines, self.columns)
 469            self.alternate = True
 470            self.buffer.clear()
 471            self.dirty.update(range(self.lines))
 472        super().set_mode(*modes, **kwargs)
 473
 474    def reset_mode(self, *modes, **kwargs):
 475        super().reset_mode(*modes, **kwargs)
 476        if kwargs.get("private") and self.alternate and {m << 5 for m in modes} & ALT_SCREEN:
 477            buffer, x, y, attrs, lines, columns = self._saved_main
 478            self.alternate = False
 479            new_size = self.lines, self.columns
 480            # Back to the main screen as it was, then reflowed if the size changed meanwhile.
 481            self.buffer.clear()
 482            self.buffer.update(buffer)
 483            self.lines, self.columns = lines, columns
 484            self.cursor.x, self.cursor.y, self.cursor.attrs = x, y, attrs
 485            self.set_margins()
 486            self.resize(*new_size)
 487            self.dirty.update(range(self.lines))
 488
 489    def write_process_input(self, data: str):
 490        self.reply(data.encode("utf-8"))
 491

 493class SafeScreen:
 494    """The screen as pyte's parser sees it. A sequence pyte can't handle
 495    (e.g. vim's "\\e[>4;2m", which pyte passes on with private=True to a
 496    method that doesn't take it) is dropped: an error inside pyte's parser
 497    would end it for good, and the terminal would show nothing more."""
 498
 499    def __init__(self, screen):
 500        self._screen = screen
 501
 502    def __getattr__(self, name):
 503        value = getattr(self._screen, name)
 504        if not callable(value):
 505            return value
 506
 507        def safe(*args, **kwargs):
 508            try:
 509                return value(*args, **kwargs)
 510            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - one odd sequence must not stop the terminal
 511                return None
 512
 513        return safe
 514
 515
 516# --------------------------------------------------------------- widget
 517def terminal_colors(palette: QPalette) -> tuple[QColor, QColor, list[str]]:
 518    """(background, text, the 16 ANSI colors) for the terminal: dark or
 519    light like the app (the ANSI colors are the Output panel's)."""
 520    if palette.color(QPalette.Base).lightness() < 128:
 521        return QColor("#1e1e1e"), QColor("#d4d4d4"), DARK
 522    return QColor("#ffffff"), QColor("#1f1f1f"), LIGHT
 523
 524
 525# pyte's color names -> index in the 16 ANSI colors.
 526ANSI_NAMES = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(
 527    ["black", "red", "green", "brown", "blue", "magenta", "cyan", "white"])}
 528ANSI_NAMES.update({"bright" + name: i + 8 for name, i in list(ANSI_NAMES.items())})
 529ANSI_NAMES.update({"yellow": 3, "brightyellow": 11})
 530ANSI_HEX = {FG_BG_256[i]: i for i in range(16)}  # (38;5;n with n < 16: the theme's colors too)
 531
 532# Keys -> what xterm sends ("{m}": the modifier parameter, when there is one).
 533CURSOR_KEYS = {Qt.Key_Up: "A", Qt.Key_Down: "B", Qt.Key_Right: "C", Qt.Key_Left: "D",
 534               Qt.Key_Home: "H", Qt.Key_End: "F"}
 535TILDE_KEYS = {Qt.Key_Insert: 2, Qt.Key_Delete: 3, Qt.Key_PageUp: 5, Qt.Key_PageDown: 6,
 536              Qt.Key_F5: 15, Qt.Key_F6: 17, Qt.Key_F7: 18, Qt.Key_F8: 19, Qt.Key_F9: 20,
 537              Qt.Key_F10: 21, Qt.Key_F11: 23, Qt.Key_F12: 24}
 538SS3_KEYS = {Qt.Key_F1: "P", Qt.Key_F2: "Q", Qt.Key_F3: "R", Qt.Key_F4: "S"}
 539# On macOS ⌘ is Qt's ControlModifier and the Control key its MetaModifier.
 540COMMAND = Qt.ControlModifier if MAC else Qt.NoModifier
 541CONTROL = Qt.MetaModifier if MAC else Qt.ControlModifier
 542PADDING = 4
 543
 544
 545class TerminalView(QWidget):
 546    """Draws a `TerminalScreen` and sends keys to the shell (see the
 547    module's description)."""
 548
 549    size_changed = Signal(int, int)  # rows, columns
 550
 551    def __init__(self, parent=None):
 552        super().__init__(parent)
 553        self.setFocusPolicy(Qt.StrongFocus)
 554        self.setAttribute(Qt.WA_OpaquePaintEvent)
 555        self.setCursor(Qt.IBeamCursor)
 556        self.setMinimumSize(80, 40)
 557        self.write = lambda data: None  # bytes to the shell (set by the panel)
 558        self.screen = TerminalScreen(80, 24)
 559        self.screen.reply = lambda data: self.write(data)
 560        self.stream = pyte.ByteStream(SafeScreen(self.screen))
 561        self.scroll_bar: QScrollBar | None = None
 562        self.hscroll_bar: QScrollBar | None = None
 563        self.word_wrap = True       # View → Word Wrap (off: a wide terminal, scrolled sideways)
 564        self._hscroll = 0           # pixels scrolled to the right (without word wrap)
 565        self._scroll = 0            # lines scrolled up from the bottom (0: following the output)
 566        self._scroll_px = 0.0       # and pixels more, into the line above (trackpad: smooth, see scroll_pixels)
 567        self._selection = None      # ((line, column), (line, column)) in all lines (scrollback + screen)
 568        self._colors: dict[str, QColor] = {}
 569        self.set_colors(QColor("#1e1e1e"), QColor("#d4d4d4"), DARK)
 570        self.set_terminal_font(QFont("Menlo" if MAC else "Monospace"))
 571        self._redraw_all = True     # (else only the rows the output changed: see _after_output)
 572        self._wheel_rest = 0.0      # part of a line scrolled, not yet moved (see wheelEvent)
 573        self._cursor_drawn_at = 0   # the screen row the cursor was last drawn on
 574        self._repaint_timer = QTimer(self)  # (output in bursts: draw at most every few ms)
 575        self._repaint_timer.setSingleShot(True)
 576        self._repaint_timer.setInterval(10)
 577        self._repaint_timer.timeout.connect(self._after_output)
 578
 579    # ------------------------------------------------------------ setup
 580    def set_colors(self, background: QColor, text: QColor, ansi: list[str]):
 581        self.background, self.foreground = QColor(background), QColor(text)
 582        self.ansi = [QColor(c) for c in ansi]
 583        self._colors.clear()
 584        self.update()
 585
 586    def set_terminal_font(self, font: QFont):
 587        # Family and size set explicitly: a size left unset would be measured
 588        # at the application's default size but drawn at the widget's.
 589        size = font.pointSizeF() if font.pointSizeF() > 0 else QApplication.font().pointSizeF()
 590        font = QFont(font)
 591        font.setFamily(font.family())
 592        font.setPointSizeF(size)
 593        font.setStyleHint(QFont.Monospace)
 594        font.setFixedPitch(True)
 595        font.setKerning(False)
 596        self.font_normal = font
 597        self.font_bold = QFont(font)
 598        self.font_bold.setBold(True)
 599        metrics = QFontMetricsF(font, self)  # (as drawn on this widget: its screen's resolution)
 600        self.cell_width = metrics.horizontalAdvance("M")
 601        self.cell_height = metrics.lineSpacing()
 602        self.ascent = metrics.ascent()
 603        self._fit()
 604        self.update()
 605
 606    def connect_scroll_bar(self, bar: QScrollBar):
 607        self.scroll_bar = bar
 608        bar.valueChanged.connect(self._scrolled)
 609        self._update_scroll_bar()
 610
 611    def connect_hscroll_bar(self, bar: QScrollBar):
 612        self.hscroll_bar = bar
 613        bar.valueChanged.connect(self._hscrolled)
 614        self._update_hscroll_bar()
 615
 616    def set_word_wrap(self, on: bool):
 617        """With word wrap the terminal is as wide as the window and long
 618        lines wrap; without, it's NO_WRAP_COLUMNS wide and the window shows
 619        part of it (the shell is told the real width either way, so line
 620        editing and full-screen programs stay right)."""
 621        self.word_wrap = on
 622        if on:
 623            self._hscroll = 0
 624        self._fit()
 625        self._update_hscroll_bar()
 626        self.update()
 627
 628    # ----------------------------------------------------------- output
 629    def feed(self, data: bytes):
 630        """Output from the shell."""
 631        before = len(self.screen.history)
 632        self.stream.feed(data)
 633        added = len(self.screen.history) - before
 634        if added:  # (lines scrolled into the scrollback: everything in view moved)
 635            self._redraw_all = True
 636        if self._scroll:  # (reading the scrollback: keep the same lines in view)
 637            self._scroll = min(self._scroll + max(0, added), len(self.screen.history))
 638        if not self._repaint_timer.isActive():
 639            self._repaint_timer.start()
 640
 641    def _after_output(self):
 642        hscroll = self._hscroll
 643        self._update_scroll_bar()
 644        self.ensure_cursor_visible()
 645        self._update_hscroll_bar()
 646        if self._redraw_all or self._scroll or self._scroll_px or self._hscroll != hscroll:
 647            self.update()  # (scrolled: every row in view is another)
 648        else:
 649            self._update_rows(set(self.screen.dirty))
 650        self._redraw_all = False
 651        self.screen.dirty.clear()
 652
 653    def _update_rows(self, rows: set[int]):
 654        """Repaint only these screen rows (what the output changed), and the
 655        cursor's old and new rows."""
 656        cursor = self.screen.cursor.y
 657        rows |= {cursor, self._cursor_drawn_at}
 658        for row in rows:
 659            if 0 <= row < self.screen.lines:
 660                top = int(PADDING + row * self.cell_height)
 661                self.update(0, top, self.width(), int(self.cell_height) + 2)
 662
 663    # ------------------------------------------------- sideways (no wrap)
 664    def _used_columns(self) -> int:
 665        """How far the text in view (and the cursor) reaches, in columns."""
 666        screen = self.screen
 667        first = len(screen.history) - self._scroll
 668        cursor_row = len(screen.history) + screen.cursor.y - first
 669        widest = screen.cursor.x + 1 if 0 <= cursor_row < screen.lines else 0
 670        blank = screen.default_char
 671        for n in range(first, first + screen.lines):
 672            line = self.line(n)
 673            if isinstance(line, list):
 674                end = len(line)
 675                while end > widest and line[end - 1] == blank:
 676                    end -= 1
 677            else:  # (a screen line: only the cells written are in it)
 678                end = max((x + 1 for x, cell in line.items() if cell != blank), default=0)
 679            widest = max(widest, min(end, screen.columns))
 680        return widest
 681
 682    def _scroll_range(self) -> int:
 683        """How far the view can scroll sideways (pixels): to the end of the
 684        widest text in view, not the terminal's full width."""
 685        if self.word_wrap:
 686            return 0
 687        return max(0, int(self._used_columns() * self.cell_width + 2 * PADDING) - self.width())
 688
 689    def _update_hscroll_bar(self):
 690        bar = self.hscroll_bar
 691        maximum = self._scroll_range()
 692        self._hscroll = min(self._hscroll, maximum)
 693        if bar is None:
 694            return
 695        bar.blockSignals(True)
 696        bar.setRange(0, maximum)
 697        bar.setPageStep(max(1, self.width()))
 698        bar.setSingleStep(max(1, int(self.cell_width * 4)))
 699        bar.setValue(self._hscroll)
 700        bar.blockSignals(False)
 701        # Shown only when there's something to scroll to; without word wrap
 702        # its room is kept while hidden, so the terminal's height (and the
 703        # shell's idea of it) doesn't change as it comes and goes.
 704        policy = bar.sizePolicy()
 705        if policy.retainSizeWhenHidden() == self.word_wrap:
 706            policy.setRetainSizeWhenHidden(not self.word_wrap)
 707            bar.setSizePolicy(policy)
 708            layout = bar.parentWidget().layout() if bar.parentWidget() else None
 709            if layout is not None:  # (a hidden widget's new policy doesn't re-lay-out by itself)
 710                layout.invalidate()
 711                layout.activate()
 712        bar.setVisible(maximum > 0)
 713
 714    def _hscrolled(self, value: int):
 715        self._hscroll = value
 716        self.update()
 717
 718    def scroll_sideways(self, pixels: int):
 719        if not self.word_wrap:
 720            self._hscroll = max(0, min(self._scroll_range(), self._hscroll + pixels))
 721            self._update_hscroll_bar()
 722            self.update()
 723
 724    def ensure_cursor_visible(self):
 725        """Without word wrap: scroll sideways to the cursor (as you type, and
 726        back to the left at a new prompt)."""
 727        if self.word_wrap or self._scroll or self._scroll_px:
 728            return
 729        x = PADDING + self.screen.cursor.x * self.cell_width
 730        margin = 4 * self.cell_width
 731        if x < self._hscroll + margin:
 732            self._hscroll = int(max(0, x - margin)) if x > self.width() - margin else 0
 733        elif x + self.cell_width > self._hscroll + self.width() - margin:
 734            self._hscroll = int(x + self.cell_width + margin - self.width())
 735        self._update_hscroll_bar()
 736
 737    def _update_scroll_bar(self):
 738        bar = self.scroll_bar
 739        if bar is None:
 740            return
 741        history = len(self.screen.history)
 742        bar.blockSignals(True)
 743        bar.setRange(0, history)
 744        bar.setPageStep(self.screen.lines)
 745        bar.setValue(history - self._scroll)
 746        bar.blockSignals(False)
 747
 748    def _scrolled(self, value: int):
 749        self._scroll = max(0, len(self.screen.history) - value)
 750        self._scroll_px = 0.0
 751        self._update_hscroll_bar()  # (the lines now in view may be wider or narrower)
 752        self.update()
 753
 754    def scroll_pixels(self, pixels: float):
 755        """Scroll the view up (positive) or down by pixels, through the
 756        scrollback: smoothly, part of a line at a time (a trackpad)."""
 757        history, ch = len(self.screen.history), self.cell_height
 758        total = max(0.0, min(history * ch, self._scroll * ch + self._scroll_px + pixels))
 759        self._scroll = min(history, int(total // ch))
 760        self._scroll_px = total - self._scroll * ch if self._scroll < history else 0.0
 761        self._update_scroll_bar()
 762        self._update_hscroll_bar()
 763        self.update()
 764
 765    def scroll_lines(self, lines: int):
 766        """Scroll the view up (positive) or down through the scrollback."""
 767        self._scroll = max(0, min(len(self.screen.history), self._scroll + lines))
 768        self._scroll_px = 0.0
 769        self._update_scroll_bar()
 770        self._update_hscroll_bar()
 771        self.update()
 772
 773    # ------------------------------------------------------------ text
 774    def total_lines(self) -> int:
 775        return len(self.screen.history) + self.screen.lines
 776
 777    def line(self, n: int):
 778        """Line ``n`` of the scrollback and screen (a list or pyte line of Chars)."""
 779        history = self.screen.history
 780        return history[n] if n < len(history) else self.screen.buffer[n - len(history)]
 781
 782    def _line_text(self, n: int, start: int = 0, end: int | None = None) -> str:
 783        line = self.line(n)
 784        width = len(line) if isinstance(line, list) else self.screen.columns
 785        end = width if end is None else min(end, width)
 786        return "".join(line[x].data for x in range(start, end)).rstrip()
 787
 788    def text(self) -> str:
 789        """All the text: the scrollback, then the screen."""
 790        lines = [self._line_text(n) for n in range(self.total_lines())]
 791        while lines and not lines[-1]:
 792            lines.pop()
 793        return "\n".join(lines)
 794
 795    def selected_text(self) -> str:
 796        if not self._selection:
 797            return ""
 798        (l1, c1), (l2, c2) = sorted(self._selection)
 799        if l1 == l2:
 800            return self._line_text(l1, c1, c2 + 1)
 801        parts = [self._line_text(l1, c1)] + [self._line_text(n) for n in range(l1 + 1, l2)]
 802        return "\n".join(parts + [self._line_text(l2, 0, c2 + 1)])
 803
 804    def _row_selection(self, n: int, width: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
 805        """The columns of line ``n`` that are selected, [start, end), or None."""
 806        if not self._selection:
 807            return None
 808        (l1, c1), (l2, c2) = sorted(self._selection)
 809        if not l1 <= n <= l2:
 810            return None
 811        return (c1 if n == l1 else 0), (c2 + 1 if n == l2 else width)
 812
 813    # ---------------------------------------------------- Edit menu, clipboard
 814    def copy(self):
 815        text = self.selected_text()
 816        if text:
 817            QApplication.clipboard().setText(text)
 818
 819    def paste(self):
 820        text = QApplication.clipboard().text()
 821        if not text:
 822            return
 823        data = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\n", "\r").encode("utf-8")
 824        if BRACKETED_PASTE in self.screen.mode:  # (so the shell doesn't run it line by line)
 825            data = b"\x1b[200~" + data + b"\x1b[201~"
 826        self._input(data)
 827
 828    def cut(self):
 829        self.copy()
 830
 831    def selectAll(self):
 832        last = self.total_lines() - 1
 833        self._selection = ((0, 0), (last, self.screen.columns - 1))
 834        self.update()
 835
 836    # (These exist so the Edit menu doesn't reach past the terminal to the editor.)
 837    def undo(self):
 838        pass
 839
 840    def redo(self):
 841        pass
 842
 843    def clear_scrollback(self):
 844        """⌘K: forget the scrollback and redraw the prompt at the top."""
 845        self.screen.history.clear()
 846        self._scroll, self._scroll_px = 0, 0.0
 847        self._selection = None
 848        self._update_scroll_bar()
 849        self._input(b"\x0c")  # Ctrl+L
 850
 851    # ------------------------------------------------------------ keys
 852    def _input(self, data: bytes):
 853        """Typing goes to the shell, and back to the bottom of the output."""
 854        if self._scroll or self._scroll_px or self._selection:
 855            self._scroll, self._scroll_px, self._selection = 0, 0.0, None
 856            self._update_scroll_bar()
 857            self.update()
 858        self.write(data)
 859
 860    def focusNextPrevChild(self, _next):
 861        return False  # Tab goes to the shell (completion), not to the next widget
 862
 863    def _wanted(self, event) -> bool:
 864        """Keys the terminal takes before the window's shortcuts: Control
 865        combinations (Ctrl+C must interrupt, not copy), Escape and Tab."""
 866        mods = event.modifiers() & ~Qt.KeypadModifier
 867        if mods & CONTROL and not mods & Qt.ShiftModifier and not (MAC and mods & COMMAND):
 868            return True
 869        return mods == Qt.NoModifier and event.key() in (Qt.Key_Escape, Qt.Key_Tab)
 870
 871    def event(self, event):
 872        if event.type() == QEvent.ShortcutOverride and self._wanted(event):
 873            event.accept()
 874            return True
 875        return super().event(event)
 876
 877    def key_bytes(self, key: int, mods, text: str) -> bytes | None:
 878        """What xterm sends for a key (None: nothing)."""
 879        shift, alt, ctrl = bool(mods & Qt.ShiftModifier), bool(mods & Qt.AltModifier), bool(mods & CONTROL)
 880        modifier = 1 + shift + 2 * alt + 4 * ctrl  # (xterm's modifier parameter)
 881        if MAC and alt and not ctrl and key in (Qt.Key_Left, Qt.Key_Right):
 882            return b"\x1bb" if key == Qt.Key_Left else b"\x1bf"  # Option+arrow: a word
 883        if key in CURSOR_KEYS:
 884            final = CURSOR_KEYS[key]
 885            if modifier > 1:
 886                return f"\x1b[1;{modifier}{final}".encode()
 887            return f"\x1b{'O' if DECCKM in self.screen.mode else '['}{final}".encode()
 888        if key in TILDE_KEYS:
 889            number = TILDE_KEYS[key]
 890            return (f"\x1b[{number};{modifier}~" if modifier > 1 else f"\x1b[{number}~").encode()
 891        if key in SS3_KEYS:
 892            return (f"\x1b[1;{modifier}{SS3_KEYS[key]}" if modifier > 1 else f"\x1bO{SS3_KEYS[key]}").encode()
 893        if key == Qt.Key_Backtab:
 894            return b"\x1b[Z"
 895        if key in (Qt.Key_Return, Qt.Key_Enter):
 896            return b"\r"
 897        if key == Qt.Key_Backspace:
 898            return b"\x08" if ctrl else b"\x7f"
 899        if key == Qt.Key_Escape:
 900            return b"\x1b"
 901        if key == Qt.Key_Tab:
 902            return b"\t"
 903        if ctrl:
 904            if Qt.Key_A <= key <= Qt.Key_Z:
 905                return bytes([key - Qt.Key_A + 1])
 906            control = {Qt.Key_Space: 0, Qt.Key_At: 0, Qt.Key_BracketLeft: 27, Qt.Key_Backslash: 28,
 907                       Qt.Key_BracketRight: 29, Qt.Key_AsciiCircum: 30, Qt.Key_Underscore: 31,
 908                       Qt.Key_Minus: 31, Qt.Key_Slash: 31}
 909            if key in control:
 910                return bytes([control[key]])
 911        if text:
 912            data = text.encode("utf-8")
 913            # Alt+key: ESC first (on macOS Option types characters instead).
 914            return b"\x1b" + data if alt and not MAC else data
 915        return None
 916
 917    def keyPressEvent(self, event):
 918        key, mods, text = event.key(), event.modifiers() & ~Qt.KeypadModifier, event.text()
 919        if MAC and mods & COMMAND:  # ⌘: the app's, not the shell's
 920            actions = {Qt.Key_C: self.copy, Qt.Key_V: self.paste, Qt.Key_K: self.clear_scrollback,
 921                       Qt.Key_A: self.selectAll}
 922            if key in actions:
 923                actions[key]()
 924            else:
 925                event.ignore()
 926            return
 927        if not MAC and mods == (Qt.ControlModifier | Qt.ShiftModifier) and key in (Qt.Key_C, Qt.Key_V):
 928            self.copy() if key == Qt.Key_C else self.paste()
 929            return
 930        if mods == Qt.ShiftModifier and key in (Qt.Key_PageUp, Qt.Key_PageDown):  # read the scrollback
 931            self.scroll_lines(self.screen.lines - 1 if key == Qt.Key_PageUp else 1 - self.screen.lines)
 932            return
 933        data = self.key_bytes(key, mods, text)
 934        if data:
 935            self._input(data)
 936        else:
 937            event.ignore()
 938
 939    # ------------------------------------------------------------ mouse
 940    def _cell_at(self, pos) -> tuple[int, int]:
 941        """(line in scrollback + screen, column) under a point."""
 942        row = int((pos.y() - PADDING - self._scroll_px) // self.cell_height)
 943        col = int((pos.x() + self._hscroll - PADDING) // self.cell_width)
 944        row = max(-1 if self._scroll_px else 0, min(self.screen.lines - 1, row))
 945        col = max(0, min(self.screen.columns - 1, col))
 946        return len(self.screen.history) - self._scroll + row, col
 947
 948    def mousePressEvent(self, event):
 949        if event.button() == Qt.LeftButton:
 950            cell = self._cell_at(event.position())
 951            self._selection = (cell, cell)
 952            self._selecting = True
 953            self.update()
 954        super().mousePressEvent(event)
 955
 956    def mouseMoveEvent(self, event):
 957        if getattr(self, "_selecting", False) and self._selection:
 958            self._selection = (self._selection[0], self._cell_at(event.position()))
 959            self.update()
 960
 961    def mouseReleaseEvent(self, event):
 962        self._selecting = False
 963        if self._selection and self._selection[0] == self._selection[1]:
 964            self._selection = None  # (a click, not a selection)
 965            self.update()
 966        elif self._selection and not MAC and sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
 967            QApplication.clipboard().setText(self.selected_text(), QClipboard.Selection)
 968
 969    def mouseDoubleClickEvent(self, event):
 970        """Select the word under the mouse."""
 971        n, x = self._cell_at(event.position())
 972        text = self._line_text(n).ljust(self.screen.columns)
 973
 974        def in_word(c):
 975            return c.isalnum() or c in "_-./~:@%+"
 976
 977        if x < len(text) and in_word(text[x]):
 978            start, end = x, x
 979            while start > 0 and in_word(text[start - 1]):
 980                start -= 1
 981            while end + 1 < len(text) and in_word(text[end + 1]):
 982                end += 1
 983            self._selection = ((n, start), (n, end))
 984            self.update()
 985
 986    def wheelEvent(self, event):
 987        """Scroll through the scrollback (or, in a full-screen program, send it
 988        arrow keys, as xterm does). A trackpad's distance is in pixels and
 989        comes in many small steps: they add up, the part of a line left over
 990        kept for the next one, so a swipe up and back down the same distance
 991        ends where it started."""
 992        pixels, angle = event.pixelDelta(), event.angleDelta()
 993        dx, dy = pixels.x() or angle.x(), pixels.y() or angle.y()
 994        if event.modifiers() & Qt.ShiftModifier:
 995            dx, dy = dx or dy, 0  # (Shift+wheel: sideways)
 996        if abs(dx) > abs(dy):  # (mostly sideways: a vertical swipe's bit of sideways doesn't count)
 997            self.scroll_sideways(-dx)
 998            return
 999        # Up and down: a trackpad in its exact pixels; a mouse wheel 3 lines a notch.
1000        distance = pixels.y() if pixels.y() else angle.y() / 120 * 3 * self.cell_height
1001        if not distance:
1002            return
1003        if not self.screen.alternate:
1004            self.scroll_pixels(distance)
1005            return
1006        # Full-screen programs: the wheel is arrow keys (as in xterm), a line at a time.
1007        self._wheel_rest += distance / max(1.0, self.cell_height)
1008        whole = int(self._wheel_rest)  # (towards zero: the rest waits for the next step)
1009        self._wheel_rest -= whole
1010        if whole:
1011            key = Qt.Key_Up if whole > 0 else Qt.Key_Down
1012            self.write(self.key_bytes(key, Qt.NoModifier, "") * abs(whole))
1013
1014    def contextMenuEvent(self, event):
1015        from qtpy.QtWidgets import QMenu
1016
1017        menu = QMenu(self)
1018        copy = menu.addAction("Copy", self.copy)
1019        copy.setEnabled(bool(self._selection))
1020        menu.addAction("Paste", self.paste)
1021        menu.addAction("Select All", self.selectAll)
1022        menu.addSeparator()
1023        menu.addAction("Clear Scrollback", self.clear_scrollback)
1024        menu.exec(event.globalPos())
1025
1026    # -------------------------------------------------------- drawing
1027    def _fit(self):
1028        """Columns and rows for the widget's size, or wider without word
1029        wrap (the shell is told)."""
1030        cols = max(2, int((self.width() - 2 * PADDING) // self.cell_width))
1031        if not self.word_wrap:
1032            cols = max(cols, NO_WRAP_COLUMNS)
1033        rows = max(1, int((self.height() - 2 * PADDING) // self.cell_height))
1034        if (rows, cols) != (self.screen.lines, self.screen.columns):
1035            self.screen.resize(rows, cols)
1036            self._scroll, self._scroll_px = min(self._scroll, len(self.screen.history)), 0.0
1037            self._update_scroll_bar()
1038            self.size_changed.emit(rows, cols)
1039
1040    def resizeEvent(self, event):
1041        super().resizeEvent(event)
1042        self._fit()
1043        self._update_hscroll_bar()
1044
1045    def focusInEvent(self, event):
1046        super().focusInEvent(event)
1047        self.update()
1048
1049    def focusOutEvent(self, event):
1050        super().focusOutEvent(event)
1051        self.update()
1052
1053    def _color(self, name: str, default: QColor) -> QColor:
1054        if name == "default":
1055            return default
1056        color = self._colors.get(name)
1057        if color is None:
1058            if name in ANSI_NAMES:
1059                color = self.ansi[ANSI_NAMES[name]]
1060            elif name in ANSI_HEX:
1061                color = self.ansi[ANSI_HEX[name]]
1062            else:
1063                color = QColor("#" + name) if len(name) == 6 else QColor(default)
1064            self._colors[name] = color
1065        return color
1066
1067    def paintEvent(self, event):
1068        painter = QPainter(self)
1069        painter.fillRect(self.rect(), self.background)
1070        offset = self._scroll_px  # (scrolled part of a line further: everything a bit lower)
1071        painter.translate(-self._hscroll, offset)  # (and sideways, without word wrap)
1072        screen = self.screen
1073        history = len(screen.history)
1074        first = history - self._scroll
1075        ch = self.cell_height
1076        palette = self.palette()
1077        select_bg = palette.color(QPalette.Highlight)
1078        select_fg = palette.color(QPalette.HighlightedText)
1079        top_row = max(-1 if offset else 0, int((event.rect().top() - PADDING - offset) // ch))
1080        bottom_row = min(screen.lines - 1, int((event.rect().bottom() - PADDING - offset) // ch))
1081        for row in range(top_row, bottom_row + 1):
1082            n = first + row
1083            if n < 0:
1084                continue
1085            line = self.line(n)
1086            width = min(len(line), screen.columns) if isinstance(line, list) else screen.columns
1087            span = self._row_selection(n, width)  # (once per row: not per cell)
1088            y = PADDING + row * ch
1089            x = 0
1090            while x < width:
1091                cell = line[x]
1092                selected = span is not None and span[0] <= x < span[1]
1093                style = (cell.fg, cell.bg, cell.bold, cell.italics, cell.underscore,
1094                         cell.strikethrough, cell.reverse, selected)
1095                start, chars = x, [cell.data]
1096                x += 1
1097                while x < width:  # (a run of cells drawn alike)
1098                    other = line[x]
1099                    if (other.fg, other.bg, other.bold, other.italics, other.underscore, other.strikethrough,
1100                            other.reverse, span is not None and span[0] <= x < span[1]) != style:
1101                        break
1102                    chars.append(other.data)
1103                    x += 1
1104                self._draw_run(painter, start, y, chars, cell, selected, select_bg, select_fg)
1105        self._draw_cursor(painter, first)
1106
1107    def _draw_run(self, painter, column, y, chars, cell, selected, select_bg, select_fg):
1108        cw, ch = self.cell_width, self.cell_height
1109        fg = self._color(cell.fg, self.foreground)
1110        bg = self._color(cell.bg, self.background)
1111        if cell.reverse:
1112            fg, bg = bg, fg
1113        if selected:
1114            fg, bg = select_fg, select_bg
1115        x0 = PADDING + column * cw
1116        if bg != self.background:
1117            painter.fillRect(QRectF(x0, y, len(chars) * cw, ch), bg)
1118        text = "".join(chars)
1119        if not text.strip():
1120            return
1121        font = self.font_bold if cell.bold else self.font_normal
1122        if cell.italics or cell.underscore or cell.strikethrough:
1123            font = QFont(font)
1124            font.setItalic(cell.italics)
1125            font.setUnderline(cell.underscore)
1126            font.setStrikeOut(cell.strikethrough)
1127        painter.setFont(font)
1128        painter.setPen(fg)
1129        baseline = y + self.ascent
1130        if text.isascii():
1131            painter.drawText(QPointF(x0, baseline), text)
1132        else:  # (each character in its cell: wide ones take two, the next is empty)
1133            for i, c in enumerate(chars):
1134                if c:
1135                    painter.drawText(QPointF(x0 + i * cw, baseline), c)
1136
1137    def _draw_cursor(self, painter, first):
1138        screen = self.screen
1139        self._cursor_drawn_at = screen.cursor.y
1140        row = len(screen.history) + screen.cursor.y - first
1141        if screen.cursor.hidden or not 0 <= row < screen.lines:
1142            return
1143        x = PADDING + screen.cursor.x * self.cell_width
1144        y = PADDING + row * self.cell_height
1145        rect = QRectF(x, y, self.cell_width, self.cell_height)
1146        if self.hasFocus():
1147            painter.fillRect(rect, self.foreground)
1148            cell = screen.buffer[screen.cursor.y][screen.cursor.x]
1149            if cell.data.strip():
1150                painter.setFont(self.font_bold if cell.bold else self.font_normal)
1151                painter.setPen(self.background)
1152                painter.drawText(QPointF(x, y + self.ascent), cell.data)
1153        else:
1154            painter.setPen(self.foreground)
1155            painter.setBrush(Qt.NoBrush)
1156            painter.drawRect(rect.adjusted(0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5))
1157

1190        layout.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)

1197    def set_directory(self, directory: Path | None):
1198        """The project's folder: where the shell starts. A different one (another
1199        project opened) restarts a running shell there; the same one (the
1200        project reloaded) leaves it alone."""
1201        directory = directory if directory and directory.is_dir() else Path.home()
1202        moved = directory.resolve() != self.directory.resolve()
1203        self.directory = directory
1204        if moved and self.shell is not None and self.shell.is_running():
1205            self.restart(focus=False)
1206        elif self.shell is None:
1207            self._update_title()
1208
1209    def _update_title(self, note: str = ""):
1210        shell = Path(user_shell()).name
1211        folder = str(self.directory).replace(str(Path.home()), "~", 1)
1212        name = environment_name()
1213        env = f" · environment <b>{name}</b>" if name else ""
1214        self.title.setText(f"<b>{shell}</b> — {folder}{env}" + (f"  <i>({note})</i>" if note else ""))
1215        self.title.setToolTip("The shell has exactly the environment VibeFPMGUI was started with "
1216                              "(your shell's startup files aren't read, so nothing changes it).")
1217
1218    def start(self):
1219        """Start the shell (if it isn't running)."""
1220        if self.shell is not None and self.shell.is_running():
1221            return
1222        view = self.view
1223        kind = WinptyShell if WINDOWS else PtyShell
1224        launch = shell_launch()
1225        self.shell = kind(launch, self.directory, view.screen.lines, view.screen.columns, self)
1226        self.shell.output.connect(view.feed)
1227        self.shell.exited.connect(self._exited)
1228        view.write = self.shell.write
1229        try:
1230            self.shell.start()
1231        except (OSError, ImportError) as exc:
1232            view.feed(f"Could not start {launch.argv[0]}: {exc}\r\n".encode())
1233            self.shell = None
1234            return
1235        self._update_title()
1236
1237    def _resized(self, rows: int, cols: int):
1238        if self.shell is not None:
1239            self.shell.resize(rows, cols)
1240
1241    def _exited(self):
1242        self._update_title("exited — Restart for a new shell")
1243        self.view.feed(b"\r\n[The shell has exited.]\r\n")
1244
1245    def restart(self, focus: bool = True):
1246        """A new shell (in ``directory``), on a clean screen."""
1247        self.shutdown()
1248        self.view.feed(b"\x1bc")  # (reset: a clean screen)
1249        self.view.screen.history.clear()
1250        self.start()
1251        if focus:
1252            self.focus()
1253
1254    def focus(self):
1255        self.view.setFocus()
1256
1257    def type_command(self, command: str):
1258        """Type ``command`` at the shell's prompt and press Return (starting
1259        the shell first if needed)."""
1260        self.start()
1261        if self.shell is not None:
1262            self.shell.write((command + "\r").encode())
1263
1264    def showEvent(self, event):
1265        super().showEvent(event)
1266        QTimer.singleShot(0, self, self.start)  # (the first time the tab is shown: after it's laid out)
1267
1268    def refresh_colors(self):
1269        self.view.set_colors(*terminal_colors(QApplication.palette()))
1270
1271    def set_font(self, font: QFont):
1272        self.view.set_terminal_font(font)
1273
1274    def set_word_wrap(self, on: bool):
1275        """View → Word Wrap (see `TerminalView.set_word_wrap`)."""
1276        self.view.set_word_wrap(on)
1277
1278    def shutdown(self):
1279        if self.shell is not None:
1280            self.shell.exited.disconnect()
1281            self.shell.stop()
1282            self.shell = None

def shell_launch() -> Launch: 
 98def shell_launch() -> Launch:
 99    """How to start the user's shell with exactly the app's environment:
100    the same variables (only TERM is set, for the terminal, and PS1, the
101    prompt), and no startup files to change them."""
102    shell = user_shell()
103    env = dict(os.environ)
104    env["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"
105    if WINDOWS:
106        return Launch([shell], env)
107    name = Path(shell).name
108    if name in PROMPTS and "PS1" not in env:  # (fish has its own prompt function)
109        active = environment_name()
110        env["PS1"] = (f"({active}) " if active else "") + PROMPTS[name]
111    return Launch([shell, *NO_STARTUP_FILES.get(name, []), "-i"], env)

114def environment_name() -> str:
115    """The activated environment the app (and the terminal) runs in, if any:
116    a pixi workspace's name (plus its environment, when not "default"), or a
117    conda environment's."""
118    pixi = os.environ.get("PIXI_PROJECT_NAME", "")
119    if pixi:
120        which = os.environ.get("PIXI_ENVIRONMENT_NAME", "default")
121        return pixi if which in ("", "default") else f"{pixi}:{which}"
122    return os.environ.get("CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV", "")

class PtyShell(PySide6.QtCore.QObject): 
126class PtyShell(QObject):
127    """A shell in a pseudo-terminal (macOS, Linux), read in the GUI thread."""
128
129    output = Signal(bytes)
130    exited = Signal()
131
132    def __init__(self, launch: Launch, cwd: Path, rows: int, cols: int, parent=None):
133        super().__init__(parent)
134        self.launch, self.cwd, self.rows, self.cols = launch, cwd, rows, cols
135        self.pid = -1
136        self.fd = -1
137        self._notifier: QSocketNotifier | None = None
138        # Input the shell hasn't taken yet (it isn't reading: a long command,
139        # a big paste); sent when the pty can take more (see _flush).
140        self._pending = bytearray()
141        self._write_notifier: QSocketNotifier | None = None
142
143    def start(self):
144        import pty
145
146        argv, env, cwd = self.launch.argv, self.launch.env, str(self.cwd)
147        program = shutil.which(argv[0]) or argv[0]
148        with warnings.catch_warnings():  # (the child only execs: fork's thread caveat doesn't apply)
149            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", DeprecationWarning)
150            pid, fd = pty.fork()
151        if pid == 0:  # the child: become the shell
152            try:
153                os.chdir(cwd)
154            except OSError:
155                pass
156            try:
157                os.execve(program, argv, env)
158            finally:
159                os._exit(127)
160        self.pid, self.fd = pid, fd
161        os.set_blocking(fd, False)
162        self.resize(self.rows, self.cols)
163        self._notifier = QSocketNotifier(fd, QSocketNotifier.Read, self)
164        self._notifier.activated.connect(self._read)
165
166    def _read(self, *_):
167        try:
168            data = os.read(self.fd, 65536)
169        except BlockingIOError:
170            return
171        except OSError:  # (Linux: EIO once the shell has exited)
172            data = b""
173        if data:
174            self.output.emit(data)
175        else:
176            self._finish()
177
178    def write(self, data: bytes):
179        """Send input to the shell, now or (what doesn't fit yet) once the
180        pty can take more: never waiting for it in the GUI thread."""
181        if self.fd < 0:
182            return
183        self._pending += data
184        self._flush()
185
186    def _flush(self, *_):
187        while self._pending and self.fd >= 0:
188            try:
189                written = os.write(self.fd, self._pending)
190            except BlockingIOError:
191                break  # (full: the rest when it's writable again)
192            except OSError:
193                self._pending.clear()
194                break
195            del self._pending[:written]
196        waiting = bool(self._pending) and self.fd >= 0
197        if waiting and self._write_notifier is None:
198            self._write_notifier = QSocketNotifier(self.fd, QSocketNotifier.Write, self)
199            self._write_notifier.activated.connect(self._flush)
200        if self._write_notifier is not None:
201            self._write_notifier.setEnabled(waiting)
202
203    def resize(self, rows: int, cols: int):
204        self.rows, self.cols = rows, cols
205        if self.fd < 0 or rows <= 0 or cols <= 0:
206            return
207        import fcntl
208        import termios
209
210        try:  # (the shell gets SIGWINCH from the kernel)
211            fcntl.ioctl(self.fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))
212        except OSError:
213            pass
214
215    def _finish(self):
216        if self._notifier is not None:
217            self._notifier.setEnabled(False)
218            self._notifier = None
219        if self._write_notifier is not None:
220            self._write_notifier.setEnabled(False)
221            self._write_notifier = None
222        self._pending.clear()
223        if self.fd >= 0:
224            try:
225                os.close(self.fd)
226            except OSError:
227                pass
228            self.fd = -1
229        if self.pid > 0:
230            try:
231                os.waitpid(self.pid, os.WNOHANG)
232            except ChildProcessError:
233                pass
234            self.pid = -1
235            self.exited.emit()
236
237    def stop(self):
238        """End the shell (and what it runs), e.g. when the window closes."""
239        pid = self.pid
240        if pid > 0:
241            for sig in (signal.SIGHUP, signal.SIGCONT):
242                try:
243                    os.kill(pid, sig)
244                except ProcessLookupError:
245                    break
246        self._finish()
247        if pid > 0:
248            def reap():  # (no zombie: force it if SIGHUP was ignored)
249                try:
250                    if os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG) == (0, 0):
251                        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
252                        os.waitpid(pid, 0)
253                except (ChildProcessError, ProcessLookupError):
254                    pass
255            QTimer.singleShot(1000, reap)
256
257    def is_running(self) -> bool:
258        return self.fd >= 0

261class WinptyShell(QObject):
262    """A shell through pywinpty (Windows ConPTY). Its reads block, so they
263    run in a thread; the output comes back to the GUI thread as a signal."""
264
265    output = Signal(bytes)

273    def start(self):
274        from winpty import PtyProcess
275
276        self._process = PtyProcess.spawn(self.launch.argv, cwd=str(self.cwd), env=self.launch.env,
277                                         dimensions=(self.rows, self.cols))
278        threading.Thread(target=self._read_loop, args=(self._process,), daemon=True,
279                         name="Terminal output").start()
280
281    def _read_loop(self, process):
282        try:
283            while True:
284                data = process.read(65536)
285                if not data and not process.isalive():
286                    break
287                if data:
288                    self.output.emit(data.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(data, str) else data)
289        except (EOFError, OSError):
290            pass
291        self.exited.emit()
292
293    def write(self, data: bytes):
294        if self._process is not None:
295            try:
296                self._process.write(data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
297            except (EOFError, OSError):
298                pass
299
300    def resize(self, rows: int, cols: int):
301        self.rows, self.cols = rows, cols
302        if self._process is not None and rows > 0 and cols > 0:
303            try:
304                self._process.setwinsize(rows, cols)
305            except (EOFError, OSError):
306                pass
307
308    def stop(self):
309        if self._process is not None:
310            try:
311                self._process.terminate(force=True)
312            except (EOFError, OSError):
313                pass
314            self._process = None
315
316    def is_running(self) -> bool:
317        return self._process is not None and self._process.isalive()

class TerminalScreen(pyte.screens.Screen): 
340class TerminalScreen(pyte.Screen):
341    """pyte's screen, with what pyte lacks: scrollback (the lines that
342    scroll off the top), the alternate screen full-screen programs draw on,
343    and reflow: lines pyte wrapped at the right edge are marked, and joined
344    and wrapped again at the new width when the terminal is resized (pyte
345    would cut them off, or leave them wrapped short)."""
346
347    def __init__(self, columns: int, lines: int):
348        self.history: deque = deque(maxlen=SCROLLBACK)  # Rows above the screen
349        self.alternate = False
350        self._saved_main = None
351        self._drawing = False
352        self.reply = lambda data: None  # answers to the terminal's queries go to the shell
353        super().__init__(columns, lines)
354
355    # ------------------------------------------------------- wrapped lines
356    def draw(self, data):
357        self._drawing = True  # (a line feed now is pyte wrapping at the right edge)
358        try:
359            super().draw(data)
360        finally:
361            self._drawing = False
362
363    def linefeed(self):
364        # Mark the row being left: wrapped (it continues on the next) or not.
365        self.buffer[self.cursor.y].wrapped = self._drawing
366        super().linefeed()
367
368    def _row(self, y: int) -> Row:
369        line = self.buffer[y]
370        row = Row(line[x] for x in range(self.columns))
371        row.wrapped = _wrapped(line)
372        if not row.wrapped:
373            while row and row[-1] == self.default_char:
374                row.pop()
375        return row
376
377    def index(self):
378        top, bottom = self.margins or pyte.screens.Margins(0, self.lines - 1)
379        if self.cursor.y == bottom and top == 0 and not self.alternate:
380            self.history.append(self._row(0))
381        super().index()
382
383    def erase_in_display(self, how=0, *args, **kwargs):
384        if how == 3:  # ("clear" also clears the scrollback)
385            self.history.clear()
386        rows = {0: range(self.cursor.y, self.lines), 1: range(self.cursor.y)}.get(how, range(self.lines))
387        for y in rows:
388            self.buffer[y].wrapped = False
389        super().erase_in_display(how, *args, **kwargs)
390
391    def erase_in_line(self, how=0, private=False):
392        if how in (0, 2):  # (the end of the line is gone: it no longer continues)
393            self.buffer[self.cursor.y].wrapped = False
394        super().erase_in_line(how, private)
395
396    # -------------------------------------------------------------- resize
397    def resize(self, lines=None, columns=None):
398        lines, columns = lines or self.lines, columns or self.columns
399        if (lines, columns) == (self.lines, self.columns):
400            return
401        if columns != self.columns:
402            # Tab stops every 8 columns across the new width (pyte sets them
403            # once, for the first width: a tab past it went to the last column).
404            self.tabstops = {x for x in self.tabstops if x < columns}
405            first_new = (min(self.columns, columns) + 7) // 8 * 8  # (the old ones stopped before the old width)
406            self.tabstops.update(range(max(8, first_new), columns, 8))
407        if self.alternate:  # (full-screen programs redraw themselves at the new size)
408            super().resize(lines, columns)
409            self.cursor.y = min(self.cursor.y, self.lines - 1)
410            self.cursor.x = min(self.cursor.x, self.columns - 1)
411            return
412        self._reflow(lines, columns)
413
414    def _reflow(self, lines: int, columns: int):
415        """Join the wrapped rows (scrollback and screen) into whole lines and
416        wrap them again at the new width, keeping the cursor on its character
417        and the bottom of the output at the bottom of the screen."""
418        last = max([self.cursor.y] + [y for y in range(self.lines) if self._row(y)])
419        rows = list(self.history) + [self._row(y) for y in range(last + 1)]
420        cursor_row = len(self.history) + self.cursor.y
421        # Whole lines (lists of Chars); where the cursor is in them.
422        logical, cursor_at = [], (0, 0)
423        current: list = []
424        for n, row in enumerate(rows):
425            if n == cursor_row:
426                cursor_at = (len(logical), len(current) + self.cursor.x)
427            current.extend(row)
428            if not row.wrapped or n == len(rows) - 1:
429                logical.append(current)
430                current = []
431        # Wrap them at the new width.
432        new_rows: list[Row] = []
433        cursor_pos = (0, 0)
434        for index, cells in enumerate(logical):
435            start_row = len(new_rows)
436            pieces = [cells[i:i + columns] for i in range(0, len(cells), columns)] or [[]]
437            for k, piece in enumerate(pieces):
438                row = Row(piece)
439                row.wrapped = k < len(pieces) - 1
440                new_rows.append(row)
441            if index == cursor_at[0]:
442                offset = cursor_at[1]
443                y, x = divmod(offset, columns)
444                if y >= len(pieces) and x == 0 and offset:  # (just past a full row: stay at its end)
445                    y, x = y - 1, columns
446                cursor_pos = (start_row + y, x)
447        while len(new_rows) <= cursor_pos[0]:
448            new_rows.append(Row())
449        top = max(0, len(new_rows) - lines, cursor_pos[0] - lines + 1)
450        top = min(top, cursor_pos[0])
451        self.history.clear()
452        self.history.extend(new_rows[:top])
453        self.buffer.clear()
454        for y, row in enumerate(new_rows[top:top + lines]):
455            line = self.buffer[y]
456            for x, char in enumerate(row):
457                line[x] = char
458            line.wrapped = row.wrapped
459        self.lines, self.columns = lines, columns
460        self.set_margins()
461        self.cursor.y = cursor_pos[0] - top
462        self.cursor.x = min(cursor_pos[1], columns)
463        self.dirty.update(range(lines))
464
465    # ---------------------------------------------------- alternate screen
466    def set_mode(self, *modes, **kwargs):
467        if kwargs.get("private") and not self.alternate and {m << 5 for m in modes} & ALT_SCREEN:
468            self._saved_main = (dict(self.buffer), self.cursor.x, self.cursor.y, self.cursor.attrs,
469                                self.lines, self.columns)
470            self.alternate = True
471            self.buffer.clear()
472            self.dirty.update(range(self.lines))
473        super().set_mode(*modes, **kwargs)
474
475    def reset_mode(self, *modes, **kwargs):
476        super().reset_mode(*modes, **kwargs)
477        if kwargs.get("private") and self.alternate and {m << 5 for m in modes} & ALT_SCREEN:
478            buffer, x, y, attrs, lines, columns = self._saved_main
479            self.alternate = False
480            new_size = self.lines, self.columns
481            # Back to the main screen as it was, then reflowed if the size changed meanwhile.
482            self.buffer.clear()
483            self.buffer.update(buffer)
484            self.lines, self.columns = lines, columns
485            self.cursor.x, self.cursor.y, self.cursor.attrs = x, y, attrs
486            self.set_margins()
487            self.resize(*new_size)
488            self.dirty.update(range(self.lines))
489
490    def write_process_input(self, data: str):
491        self.reply(data.encode("utf-8"))

Erases display in a specific way.

Character attributes are set to cursor attributes.

Parameters

  • int how: defines the way the line should be erased in:

    • 0 -- Erases from cursor to end of screen, including cursor position.
    • 1 -- Erases from beginning of screen to cursor, including cursor position.
    • 2 and 3 -- Erases complete display. All lines are erased and changed to single-width. Cursor does not move.
  • bool private: when True only characters marked as erasable are affected not implemented.

Changed in version 0.8.1: The method accepts any number of positional arguments as some clear implementations include a ; after the first parameter causing the stream to assume a 0 second parameter.

Resize the screen to the given size.

If the requested screen size has more lines than the existing screen, lines will be added at the bottom. If the requested size has less lines than the existing screen lines will be clipped at the top of the screen. Similarly, if the existing screen has less columns than the requested screen, columns will be added at the right, and if it has more -- columns will be clipped at the right.

Parameters
  • int lines: number of lines in the new screen.
  • int columns: number of columns in the new screen.

Changed in version 0.7.0: If the requested screen size is identical to the current screen size, the method does nothing.

class SafeScreen: 
494class SafeScreen:
495    """The screen as pyte's parser sees it. A sequence pyte can't handle
496    (e.g. vim's "\\e[>4;2m", which pyte passes on with private=True to a
497    method that doesn't take it) is dropped: an error inside pyte's parser
498    would end it for good, and the terminal would show nothing more."""
499
500    def __init__(self, screen):
501        self._screen = screen
502
503    def __getattr__(self, name):
504        value = getattr(self._screen, name)
505        if not callable(value):
506            return value
507
508        def safe(*args, **kwargs):
509            try:
510                return value(*args, **kwargs)
511            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - one odd sequence must not stop the terminal
512                return None
513
514        return safe
